name: read_dtlb_virtual
prose: Executes the Xtensa rdtlb0 instruction on the data-TLB entry selected by the int argument way and returns the raw register result as an unsigned long. According to the header comment, in the Linux configuration bits 31..12 of the result hold the virtual address, bits 11..08 are meaningless and bits 07..00 hold the ASID. The function does not validate way (the same header invalidates way numbers up to DTLB_WAY_PGD+2, so a 0..7 range is not established by this code), has no error return, and takes no locks or references; the asm operand for way is declared read-write ('+a') but way is a by-value parameter, so only the local copy can be altered, not the caller's variable.
note: Reviewer round 15 right on both points: tlbflush.h:179 way is a by-value int so '+a' cannot clobber the caller's variable; tlbflush.h:15,146 DTLB_WAY_PGD=7 and DTLB_WAY_PGD+2 is used, so the 0..7 range claim is unsupported. Bit layout is from the comment at tlbflush.h:171-174.

name: read_itlb_virtual
prose: Executes the Xtensa ritlb0 instruction on the instruction-TLB entry selected by the int argument way and returns the raw register result as an unsigned long. According to the header comment, in the Linux configuration bits 31..12 of the result hold the virtual address, bits 11..08 are meaningless and bits 07..00 hold the ASID. The function does not validate way (no valid range is established by this code), has no error return, and takes no locks or references; the asm operand for way is declared read-write ('+a') but way is a by-value parameter, so only the local copy can be altered, not the caller's variable.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: tlbflush.h:193 way is by-value so '+a' only affects the local copy; no ITLB way range is checked or documented in the function.

name: xtensa_pmu_cache_event
prose: Decodes the 64-bit config as cache_type = bits 7..0, cache_op = bits 15..8 and cache_result = bits 23..16 (higher bits are ignored). It returns -EINVAL if cache_type >= ARRAY_SIZE(xtensa_cache_ctl) (5 rows: L1D=0, L1I=1, LL=2, DTLB=3, ITLB=4), if cache_op >= 3 (PERF_COUNT_HW_CACHE_OP_MAX) or if cache_result >= 2 (RESULT_MAX). Otherwise it reads xtensa_cache_ctl[cache_type][cache_op][cache_result] and returns -EINVAL when that entry is 0 (entries the table does not initialise: the whole LL row, the prefetch op, and any op other than read for L1I, DTLB and ITLB), else returns the entry, which is a PMU control word built by XTENSA_PMU_MASK(select, mask): L1D read access/miss use select 10 with masks 0x1/0x2, L1D write select 11 with 0x1/0x2, L1I read select 8 with 0x1/0x2, DTLB read select 9 with 0x1/0x8, ITLB read select 7 with 0x1/0x8. It only reads the constant table and takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: Contract left empty: reads a static table and the previous contract attempts failed mechanical checks. Table values checked at perf_event.c:80-111, function at :113-133.

name: do_signal
prose: Called on return to user mode with regs. It first sets task_pt_regs(current)->icountlevel to 0. If get_signal(&ksig) reports a signal: when regs->syscall != NO_SYSCALL it adjusts the interrupted system call result in regs->areg[2] before building the frame (-ERESTARTNOHAND and -ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK become -EINTR; -ERESTARTSYS becomes -EINTR if the handler lacks SA_RESTART, otherwise, like -ERESTARTNOINTR, areg[2] is set to regs->syscall and regs->pc is moved back by 3; other values are left alone); it then calls setup_frame(&ksig, sigmask_to_save(), regs) and passes its return value to signal_setup_done(ret, &ksig, 0) (setup_frame returns -EFAULT before rewriting the handler registers if it cannot build the frame, and signal_setup_done then forces a SIGSEGV for a failed delivery), sets icountlevel to 1 if TIF_SINGLESTEP is set, and returns. If no signal is reported: when regs->syscall != NO_SYSCALL and areg[2] is -ERESTARTNOHAND, -ERESTARTSYS or -ERESTARTNOINTR it sets areg[2] to regs->syscall and moves pc back by 3, or for -ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK sets areg[2] to __NR_restart_syscall and moves pc back by 3; no -EINTR is written on this path; it then calls restore_saved_sigmask(), sets icountlevel to 1 if TIF_SINGLESTEP is set, and returns. The function returns void.
note: Reviewer round 15 wrong: icountlevel=1 for TIF_SINGLESTEP is set on both exits (signal.c:496-497 and 522-523). Reviewer round 2 partly right but prose already covered it; restart adjustment happens before setup_frame regardless of its result (signal.c:464-490 then 494). setup_frame returns -EFAULT at :359,374,407 before regs are rewritten at :415-434. Removed unverified 'caller holds no locks'.

name: aie2_init
prose: Probe-time initialisation of the AIE2 NPU for xdna. It returns -EINVAL immediately if hypervisor_is_type(X86_HYPER_NATIVE) is false, and -ENOMEM if the drmm_kzalloc of the device handle fails. It then calls request_firmware; if that fails its errno is returned directly (no firmware was obtained, so there is nothing to release). After the firmware has been obtained, the following failures all release the firmware with release_firmware and return the error: pcim_enable_device (its errno), a NULL pcim_iomap of a needed BAR (-ENOMEM), dma_set_mask_and_coherent (its errno), pci_msix_vec_count <= 0 (-EINVAL), pci_alloc_irq_vectors < 0 (its negative errno), aie2m_psp_create returning NULL (-ENOMEM), and aie2_hw_start failing (its errno). If xrsm_init returns NULL it returns -EINVAL after calling aie2_hw_stop and then release_firmware. xdna->dev_handle is assigned once the PSP context exists and is not reset on the later error paths. On success it stores the resolver in xdna->xrs_hdl, releases the firmware, calls amdxdna_pm_init(xdna) (return value not used) and returns 0. The function does not itself free the IRQ vectors, BAR mappings or PSP context on its error paths.
note: Slice cut the head (function starts at aie2_pci.c:482). Reviewer round 15 right: request_firmware failure returns directly (aie2_pci.c:505-510) without release_firmware; prose rewritten. Earlier prose also wrongly implied the firmware is released in that case.

name: hl_cs_ctx_switch
prose: Handles the context-switch / restore phase before a command submission for hpriv->ctx, writing the restore command submission's sequence number through cs_seq when one is submitted. If hdev->supports_ctx_switch it atomically swaps ctx->thread_ctx_switch_token from 1 to 0 and uses the old value as do_ctx_switch. When do_ctx_switch is nonzero or args->in.cs_flags has HL_CS_FLAGS_FORCE_RESTORE: it takes hpriv->restore_phase_mutex; if do_ctx_switch it calls hdev->asic_funcs->context_switch(hdev, ctx->asid) and on failure logs, records need_soft_reset when the error is -ETIMEDOUT or -EBUSY, unlocks the mutex and goes to the exit with that error (cs_seq untouched); then it calls restore_phase_topology and, if args->in.num_chunks_restore is 0, sets rc to 0, otherwise calls cs_ioctl_default (which sets *cs_seq to ULLONG_MAX on entry, to the restore CS sequence on success, and back to ULLONG_MAX on its own failures). It then unlocks the mutex; if the submission failed it logs and exits with that error. If a restore CS was submitted it waits for it with _hl_cs_wait_ioctl and on failure exits with -ENOEXEC (*cs_seq still holds the restore sequence). Otherwise, with supports_ctx_switch, it sets ctx->thread_ctx_switch_wait_token to 1. In the remaining case (no context switch and no forced restore) when supports_ctx_switch is set and thread_ctx_switch_wait_token is still 0 it polls that token until it equals 1 with hl_poll_timeout_memory; -ETIMEDOUT is logged and returned, and any other poll result is returned as is. At the exit, hl_device_reset(hdev, 0) is called only if the result is -ETIMEDOUT or -EBUSY and need_soft_reset was set, which can only happen for a context_switch failure; the poll timeout and a cs_ioctl_default error do not trigger it. The function returns rc: 0 when nothing needed doing, when the poll succeeded, when the restore CS was empty or when the restore completed. The restore_phase_mutex is not held when it returns.
note: Reviewer claims (rounds 0 and 2) already reflected: *cs_seq untouched when no restore CS submitted, ULLONG_MAX set by cs_ioctl_default (command_submission.c:1507-1508, 1676), restore seq kept on -ENOEXEC wait failure (hl_cs_ctx_switch :1754-1763). Mutex unlocked at :1722 and :1741 only; reset only via need_soft_reset set at :1720-1721. Rewritten for clarity and enumerated exits.

name: hl_read
prose: hwmon read callback: takes the hl_device from dev_get_drvdata(dev). It returns -ENODEV if hl_device_operational(hdev, NULL) is false. Otherwise it computes use_cpucp_enum from hdev->asic_prop.fw_app_cpu_boot_dev_sts0 & CPU_BOOT_DEV_STS0_MAP_HWMON_EN and switches on type: hwmon_temp (input, max, crit, max_hyst, crit_hyst, offset, highest), hwmon_in (input, min, max, highest), hwmon_curr (input, min, max, highest), hwmon_fan (input, min, max), hwmon_pwm (input, enable) and hwmon_power (input, input_highest). For an unsupported attr within one of those types, or an unsupported type, it returns -EINVAL. For a supported pair it maps attr to the CPUCP attribute (or, when use_cpucp_enum is false, passes the legacy attribute fixed up by fixup_attr_legacy_fw, except pwm which passes attr unchanged) and returns whatever hl_get_temperature, hl_get_voltage, hl_get_current, hl_get_fan_speed, hl_get_pwm_info or hl_get_power returns for hdev, channel, the attribute and val; whether *val is written is up to that callee. It takes no locks itself.
note: Reviewer round 15 wrong: hl_read does check operational state and returns -ENODEV (hwmon.c:251-252). Prose kept; softened the claim about *val being set to what the callees do. Function body at hwmon.c:243-395.

name: gaudi_memset_registers
prose: Fills a kernel command buffer with num_regs PACKET_MSG_LONG write packets (ctl with the opcode, EB, RB and MB bits set, value val, address reg_base + i*4 for i = 0..num_regs-1) and submits it as a job on queue GAUDI_QUEUE_ID_DMA_0_0 via gaudi_send_job_on_qman0. cb_size is computed in a u32 as sizeof(struct packet_msg_long) * num_regs + sizeof(struct packet_msg_prot) (the trailing packet_msg_prot space is reserved but not written by this function). It returns -ENOMEM, with an error log and no allocation, if cb_size exceeds SZ_2M; -EFAULT if hl_cb_kernel_create returns NULL; -ENOMEM if hl_cs_allocate_job fails, in which case the buffer is released with hl_cb_put and hl_cb_destroy (no job exists); otherwise it sets up the job, adds it to debugfs, calls gaudi_send_job_on_qman0, removes the job from debugfs, kfree()s it, decrements the buffer's cs_cnt, calls hl_cb_put and hl_cb_destroy on the buffer and returns the status of gaudi_send_job_on_qman0 (0 or a negative error).
note: Reviewer round 15 right that there is no precondition: oversize requests are handled by the -ENOMEM return (gaudi.c:5671-5674). Rounds 1 and 2 claims fit the early returns (:5673,5678) which do skip the cleanup; prose lists each exit separately. Note cb_size u32 truncation (:5669).

name: gaudi_set_hbm_bar_base
prose: Moves the HBM BAR inbound region and returns the previous base, or U64_MAX on failure. With gaudi = hdev->asic_specific (may be NULL): if gaudi is non-NULL and gaudi->hbm_bar_cur_addr equals addr it returns addr at once without touching hardware (this check comes first, so it applies even when iatu_done_by_fw is set). Otherwise, if hdev->asic_prop.iatu_done_by_fw is true it returns U64_MAX. Otherwise it fills a PCI_BAR_MATCH_MODE region for HBM_BAR_ID at addr and calls hl_pci_set_inbound_region(hdev, 2, &region); if that fails it returns U64_MAX and leaves gaudi->hbm_bar_cur_addr unchanged (whatever the failed call did to the hardware is outside this function). On success, if gaudi is non-NULL it saves the old hbm_bar_cur_addr, stores addr in it and returns the old value; if gaudi is NULL it returns addr.
note: Reviewer rounds 1 and 15: round 15 wrong in effect, the prose already put the cache-hit return first; round 1 right that iatu_done_by_fw returns U64_MAX (gaudi.c:733-737). Replaced 'without any side effect' on the set-region failure with the narrower claim about hbm_bar_cur_addr.

name: gaudi2_handle_eqe
prose: Handles one event-queue entry from the gaudi2 firmware; returns void. It decodes event_type from eq_entry->hdr.ctl. If event_type >= GAUDI2_EVENT_SIZE it logs an error and returns without updating any counters. Otherwise it increments gaudi2->events_stat[event_type] and events_stat_aggregate[event_type] and runs a switch on event_type whose cases call the class-specific handlers (ECC, QMAN, ARC, SEI, PCIe, SM, ...) or set values directly, updating event_mask, reset_flags, reset_required, is_critical and error_count; the default case only logs an error when the event's gaudi2_irq_map_table entry is marked valid. After the switch it calls hl_capture_engine_err when the event mask has HL_NOTIFIER_EVENT_USER_ENGINE_ERR, prints the event if error_count is GAUDI2_NA_EVENT_CAUSE and the event is not an info event, or prints a no-error-cause message if error_count is 0. If the event's table entry has a reset type other than EVENT_RESET_TYPE_NONE or reset_required is set, it adds HL_DRV_RESET_HARD when reset_required or the table says HARD; and if hdev->hard_reset_on_fw_events is set, or fw_security_enabled with is_critical, it takes the reset path: it adds BYPASS_REQ_TO_FW plus DEVICE_UNAVAILABLE for the fw-security critical case, otherwise HL_DRV_RESET_DELAY, calls hl_handle_critical_hw_err for general-HW-error events, dumps the config access history, adds HL_NOTIFIER_EVENT_DEVICE_RESET and calls hl_device_cond_reset(hdev, reset_flags, event_mask), and returns without unmasking the interrupt or calling hl_notifier_event_send_all here. Otherwise it unmasks the interrupt with hl_fw_unmask_irq unless the table entry is flagged msg, sends the notifier event if event_mask is non-zero, and returns.
note: Real function name is gaudi2_handle_eqe (gaudi2.c:10143); packet name gaudi2_handle_eq_event does not exist. Slice cut the tail (function ends at :10629). Systematic: name differs from file.

name: pm_mng_profile_store
prose: sysfs store handler for the Goya power-management profile; hdev comes from dev_get_drvdata(dev) and goya from hdev->asic_specific. If hl_device_operational(hdev, NULL) is false it returns -ENODEV without taking any lock. Otherwise it takes hdev->fpriv_list_lock; if hdev->is_compute_ctx_active it logs and returns -EPERM after releasing the lock. If buf starts with the 4 characters 'auto' (strncmp against strlen), then only when goya->pm_mng_profile is PM_MANUAL it sets goya->curr_pll_profile to PLL_HIGH, pm_mng_profile to PM_AUTO and calls goya_set_frequency(hdev, PLL_LOW) while holding the lock; the lock is then released and count returned. If buf starts with 'manual', then only when pm_mng_profile is PM_AUTO it sets pm_mng_profile to PM_MANUAL, releases the lock, flushes goya->goya_work->work_freq with flush_delayed_work when goya->goya_work is non-NULL, and returns count; if it was already PM_MANUAL the lock is released and count returned. If buf starts with neither it logs 'value should be auto or manual', releases the lock and returns -EINVAL. On each return the lock is not held. Operational state and absence of an active compute context are checked by the function, not required of the caller.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: -ENODEV / -EPERM are handled (goya_hwmgr.c:257-269). Previous prose put these as preconditions; rewritten with each exit listed. Function at goya_hwmgr.c:251-306.

name: ivpu_debugfs_init
prose: Creates the ivpu debugfs entries for vdev under vdev->drm.debugfs_root and returns void. It registers the vdev_debugfs_list files with drm_debugfs_add_files, then creates (with debugfs_create_file, whose results are not checked) force_recovery, dvfs_mode, fw_dyndbg, fw_log, fw_trace_destination_mask, fw_trace_hw_comp_mask, fw_trace_level, hws_priority_bands, reset_engine and resume_engine; the fw_profiling_freq_drive and dct files are created only when ivpu_hw_ip_gen(vdev) >= IVPU_HW_IP_40XX, and the fail_hw fault-injection attribute is created only when CONFIG_FAULT_INJECTION is defined.
note: Slice cut the head: the function starts at ivpu_debugfs.c:481 as void ivpu_debugfs_init(struct ivpu_device *vdev); packet marked it dropped but it is a real function, so fixed.

name: ivpu_mmu_context_unmap_sgt
prose: Unmaps the scatter-gather table sgt from ctx's page tables, starting at VPU address vpu_addr, and returns void. If ctx is NULL it fires drm_WARN_ON and returns without doing anything. Otherwise it takes ctx->lock and, for each DMA segment of sgt in order, computes size = sg_dma_len(sg) + sg->offset (the dma_addr sg_dma_address(sg) - sg->offset is only used in the debug message), calls ivpu_mmu_context_unmap_pages(ctx, vpu_addr, size), which unmaps one IVPU_MMU_PAGE_SIZE page at a time while size is non-zero, and then advances vpu_addr by size. After the loop it issues wmb(), releases ctx->lock and calls ivpu_mmu_invalidate_tlb(vdev, ctx->id); a failure of that call is only reported with ivpu_warn. Note that unmap_pages subtracts a full page size from size each step and so assumes each segment size is a multiple of the page size.
note: Real name is ivpu_mmu_context_unmap_sgt (ivpu_mmu_context.c:499-530); packet name ivpu_mmu_context_unmap does not exist. Fixed earlier wrong claim that each range begins at sg_dma_address - offset: unmapping uses the running vpu_addr (:515-520).

name: speakup_kobj_init
prose: Module-init helper that creates the speakup sysfs tree and takes no parameters. It creates a kobject 'accessibility' with no parent (kobject_create_and_add) and stores it in accessibility_kobj, then creates 'speakup' under it, stored in speakup_kobj, and registers main_attr_group and then i18n_attr_group on speakup_kobj. It returns 0 if all of these succeed. It returns -ENOMEM if either kobject_create_and_add returns NULL, and otherwise the errno of a failing sysfs_create_group. On failure it unwinds only what it created: if the first group fails it kobject_puts speakup_kobj and then accessibility_kobj; if the second group fails it first removes main_attr_group, then does the same two puts; if the speakup kobject creation fails it puts accessibility_kobj; if the accessibility creation fails nothing needs releasing. The global pointers accessibility_kobj and speakup_kobj are not reset to NULL on the failure paths.
note: Slice head missing (function starts at kobjects.c:1004). Prior prose assumed global pointers unset at entry (not checked in code) and said it released every reference; failure paths do not NULL the globals. Contract removed: function writes globals.

name: spkup_write
prose: Feeds count characters from in_buf (u16 values) to the synthesizer; returns void. On entry it sets spk_keydown to 0; static variables rep_count, ch, old_ch, char_type and last_type keep state between calls. For each character: when cursor_track == read_all_mode and the current in_buf pointer equals sentmarks[bn][currsentence] and currsentence <= numsentences[bn], it inserts a sentence index with synth_insert_next_index(currsentence++). The character's type is spk_chartab[ch] for ch < 0x100, else ALPHA. If ch equals old_ch and is not a B_NUM type, rep_count is incremented and when it then exceeds 2 (that is, from the fourth consecutive identical character on) the character is skipped entirely (old_ch and last_type are not updated); otherwise (different character, or a numeric one) a pending repeat is announced first if last_type has CH_RPT and rep_count > 2, as a space, MSG_REPEAT_DESC formatted with ++rep_count, and a space, and rep_count is reset to 0. The character is then handled by the first matching case: if it equals spk_lastkey, rep_count is reset and the character is spoken with speak_char only when spk_key_echo == 1 and ch >= MINECHOCHAR; else B_ALPHA characters go to synth_putwc_s (preceded by a SPACE when SF_DEC is set and last_type has PUNC); else B_NUM characters reset rep_count and go to synth_putwc_s; else characters matching spk_punc_mask are spoken with speak_char and have PUNC cleared from the stored type; else SYNTH_OK characters are sent with synth_putwc_s only when they differ from old_ch, otherwise rep_count is reset; else a SPACE is added when old_ch differs from ch, otherwise rep_count is reset. old_ch and last_type are then set to the character and its type. After the loop spk_lastkey is set to 0; if count was above 2 on entry and rep_count > 2 it announces MSG_REPEAT_DESC2 (with ++rep_count) when last_type has CH_RPT, and resets rep_count to 0. It takes no lock and keeps no reference to in_buf.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: third consecutive identical char is still output, suppression starts at the fourth (main.c:1099-1101: rep_count goes 1,2,3). Rounds 0 and 2 (numeric not collapsed, spk_lastkey special case, sentmarks bound) incorporated. Function at main.c:1079-1157.

name: spell_word
prose: Spells the word under the cursor character by character; returns void. It calls get_word(vc); if that returns 0 the function returns at once (get_word returns 0 after printing MSG_SPACE when spk_say_word_ctl is set and the character under the cursor is a SPACE; no spelling output is produced by spell_word itself). Otherwise it iterates over the NUL-terminated word get_word placed in buf. Before each character except the first it prints ' <delay_str[spk_spell_delay]> '. For a capital (ch < 0x100 and IS_CHAR(ch, B_CAP)) it selects spk_str_caps_start and, if spk_str_caps_stop is non-empty, increments spk_pitch_shift, but if spk_str_caps_stop is empty it resets the remembered caps state so that spk_str_caps_start is printed before every capital (it is printed only when that selection differs from the remembered one); for a non-capital it selects spk_str_caps_stop, which is printed only when the remembered state was caps-start. The character is sent to the synthesizer as a wide character when ch >= 0x100 or the DIRECT variable is non-zero; as the phonetic name phonetic[(ch & 0x1f) - 1] when this_speakup_key == SPELL_PHONETIC and ch is an ASCII letter; otherwise as spk_characters[ch], printing MSG_CTRL first and skipping the '^' when the string starts with '^'. After the loop, if the last selected string was not spk_str_caps_stop, it prints spk_str_caps_stop.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: with an empty spk_str_caps_stop, last_cap is reset on each capital (main.c:719-722), so caps_start is printed before every capital; the old prose said it was never printed. Round 2 claim (only on transition) holds only when caps_stop is non-empty; round 0 claim (get_word can print MSG_SPACE) right and prose already says so (main.c:555-558). Function at main.c:701-749.

name: testkernel
prose: Probes the DECtalk card at speakup_info.port_tts. It reads the status with dt_getstatus(); if the value is 0xffff it sets status -1 and jumps to the cleanup. Otherwise it sends CMD_sync with dt_sendcmd and waits for STAT_cmd_ready with dt_waitbit; if the bit does not appear status becomes -2 but is then overwritten with -3 (the assignment after the if/else chain). If the bit appears and dt_stat has bit 0x8000 set, it returns 0 without releasing anything, so the I/O region stays requested and port_tts is unchanged. If the bit appears but dt_stat does not have bit 0x8000 set, it prints a warning that the software is not loaded when dt_stat equals 0x0dec, and sets status -3. On the -1 and -3 outcomes it calls synth_release_region(speakup_info.port_tts, SYNTH_IO_EXTENT), sets speakup_info.port_tts to 0 and returns the status. So the possible results are 0, -1 and -3; -2 is not returned. It takes no lock.
note: Reviewer round 1 right that -2 is overwritten by -3 (speakup_decpc.c:362,368); prose already said so. Round 15 about contract: contract removed because the function reads and writes global state and performs I/O. Function at :352-372.

name: do_catch_up
prose: Kernel-thread worker that drains the speakup buffer to the KeyPC synthesizer port; returns void. It reads the jiffy, delay and full-time variables via spk_get_var, reads the JIFFY value under speakup_info.spinlock and computes jiff_max. It loops while kthread_should_stop() is false: under the spinlock, if speakup_info.flushing is set it clears the flag, unlocks, calls synth->flush(synth) and continues; otherwise it skips non-Latin-1 characters, and if the buffer is empty it unlocks and leaves the loop. Otherwise it reads the full-time value, unlocks, and if synth_full() (status bit 0x80 clear) it sleeps for full_time milliseconds and continues. Else it polls with while (synth_writable()) up to 1000 iterations (synth_writable() is true while status bit 0x10 is set, so this waits for that bit to clear); if the 1000 iterations are used up it calls oops() (which logs a warning with four port reads and returns NULL, result ignored) and leaves the loop. Otherwise it takes the next buffer byte under the spinlock, maps the newline character to PROCSPEECH, writes it to synth_port with outb_p and delays 70 microseconds. If jiffies has reached jiff_max and the byte was SPACE, it polls the port the same way (oops and leave the loop on timeout), writes PROCSPEECH, re-reads the jiffy and delay values under the spinlock, sleeps for delay_time milliseconds and sets a new jiff_max. After the loop (whether it ended through kthread stop, an empty buffer or a timeout) it polls once more up to 1000 iterations and, if the port became ready, writes PROCSPEECH; if the poll times out it calls oops() and writes nothing. Each spinlock acquisition is released before the next step in the same iteration, and the function holds no lock when it returns. A timeout exit can leave data in the buffer and does not stop the thread.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the final PROCSPEECH is written when synth_writable() returns false (i.e. wait for status bit 0x10 to clear) (speakup_keypc.c:130-133, 248-255). Round 2 right that oops() only logs (:140-150) and the loop then runs the final poll. Round 0 right on timeout break (:219-222). Function at :173-256.

name: acpi_aml_open
prose: File open handler for the ACPI AML debugger interface. It takes acpi_aml_io.lock and returns -EBUSY if acpi_aml_io.flags has ACPI_AML_CLOSED. For a file not opened write-only, it returns -EBUSY if acpi_aml_active_reader is already set, else records this file as acpi_aml_active_reader. For a write-only open it returns -ENODEV if ACPI_AML_OPENED is not set. If this file is the active reader it drops the mutex, calls acpi_initialize_debugger, and on failure returns -EINVAL without retaking the mutex and without clearing acpi_aml_active_reader (the error path jumps past the clearing code, so the file stays recorded as the active reader). On success it retakes the mutex, sets ACPI_AML_OPENED, and zeroes the head and tail of out_crc and in_crc. For the successful cases it increments acpi_aml_io.users and returns 0 (a write-only open of an already opened interface does not touch the rings or the active reader). When it fails with -EBUSY or -ENODEV, acpi_aml_active_reader is cleared if it equals this file, and the mutex is released; on the -EINVAL path the mutex was already released before the call.
note: Reviewer round 15 wrong: on -EINVAL the code does goto err_exit (acpi_dbg.c:507), which skips the err_lock block (:518-522) that clears acpi_aml_active_reader, so the file stays recorded; prose kept. Round 2 (thread-creation errors) is covered by the -EINVAL case. Function at :462-526. Mutex is dropped during acpi_initialize_debugger.

name: acpi_format_ipmi_request
prose: Builds the IPMI request message in tx_msg from an ACPI IPMI opregion access. It first sets tx_msg->tx_message.netfn to (address >> 8) & 0xff, cmd to address & 0xff and the message data pointer to tx_msg->data, and treats value as a pointer to an acpi_ipmi_buffer. If buffer->length is greater than ACPI_IPMI_MAX_MSG_LENGTH it warns once and returns -EINVAL; at that point netfn, cmd and the data pointer have already been written but data_len, the data copy, the address fields and tx_msgid have not. Otherwise it sets data_len to buffer->length, copies that many bytes from buffer->data into tx_msg->data, sets the address to IPMI_SYSTEM_INTERFACE_ADDR_TYPE with channel IPMI_BMC_CHANNEL and data[0] = 0, then under device->tx_msg_lock (spin_lock_irqsave) increments device->curr_msgid, stores it in tx_msg->tx_msgid, releases the lock and returns 0.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: netfn/cmd/data are written before the length check (acpi_ipmi.c:258-260, 269-274); earlier prose said tx_msg unmodified. Function at :243-298.

name: acpi_db_create_execution_threads
prose: Debugger helper that runs a control method from several threads; returns void. It parses num_threads_arg and num_loops_arg with strtoul(..., 0); if either is 0 it prints a 'Bad argument' message and returns. It then creates three semaphores (main_thread_gate with initial count 0, thread_complete_gate and info_gate with initial count 1); if any creation fails it prints a message, deletes the ones already created, and returns. It zeroes the global acpi_gbl_db_method_info, sets num_threads, allocates and zeroes an array of acpi_thread_id with one entry per thread into acpi_gbl_db_method_info.threads (on allocation failure it prints a message, deletes the three semaphores and returns), then fills in the name (method_name_arg is stored by pointer, not copied), loop count, semaphores and argument tables. It calls acpi_db_execute_setup and then acpi_get_handle for the pathname; if either fails it jumps to the cleanup without starting threads (this function prints a diagnostic only for the acpi_get_handle failure; acpi_db_execute_setup may print its own). Otherwise it prints a 'Creating ... threads' message and calls acpi_os_execute for up to num_threads threads, stopping the loop at the first failure, then waits on main_thread_gate with ACPI_WAIT_FOREVER and prints 'All threads (...) have completed'. The cleanup (reached on the setup and handle failures and after the wait) deletes the three semaphores, frees the thread-id array and sets acpi_gbl_db_method_info.threads to NULL.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: acpi_db_execute_setup failure goes straight to cleanup_and_exit with no message from this function (dbexec.c:826-829); old prose said it prints a diagnostic. The final wait has no timeout, so if no thread was started (acpi_os_execute failing at i=0) the wait on main_thread_gate would not be satisfied by any thread. Function at :719-875.

name: acpi_db_evaluate_one_predefined_name
prose: Namespace-walk callback that evaluates one predefined ACPI name; context is a struct acpi_db_execute_walk with count and max_count. It returns AE_OK with nothing done if the node name does not match a predefined method (acpi_ut_match_predefined_method), if the node type is ACPI_TYPE_LOCAL_SCOPE, or if acpi_ns_get_normalized_pathname returns NULL. If acpi_get_object_info fails it frees the pathname and returns that status. Otherwise, if the object is a method, it fills a local params array with the arg_count default arguments that ACPI requires taken from the predefined info (Integer value 1, a default String, a 48-byte Buffer pointing at the params array itself, an empty Package; an unsupported type is only reported with acpi_os_printf) and points param_objects at it; for non-methods param_objects stays empty. It frees obj_info, sets acpi_gbl_method_executing to TRUE, calls acpi_evaluate_object(node, NULL, &param_objects, &return_obj) with ACPI_ALLOCATE_BUFFER, prints the pathname and the returned exception text, sets the flag back to FALSE, frees pathname, ignores the evaluation status, increments info->count, and returns AE_CTRL_TERMINATE if info->count >= info->max_count, otherwise AE_OK. Any buffer allocated into return_obj is not freed here.
note: Slice cut the head; real function is acpi_db_evaluate_one_predefined_name (dbtest.c:965-1104), not acpi_db_execute_method (which lives in dbexec.c). Earlier prose omitted the three early AE_OK returns. Systematic: packet name wrong.

name: acpi_db_single_step
prose: Called before each AML op executes to implement single-step and breakpoints. In builds without ACPI_APPLICATION it returns AE_OK at once if the current thread is not acpi_gbl_db_thread_id. It then returns AE_ABORT_METHOD after clearing acpi_gbl_abort_method if that flag was set. It computes aml_offset of op within the method. If walk_state->method_breakpoint is non-zero and not greater than aml_offset, it prints a '***Break***' message, sets acpi_gbl_cm_single_step to TRUE, clears acpi_gbl_step_to_next_call and zeroes walk_state->method_breakpoint; else if walk_state->user_breakpoint equals aml_offset exactly it prints '***UserBreakpoint***' and does the same three updates (user_breakpoint itself is left unchanged). After the breakpoint checks it returns AE_OK for AML_INT_NAMEDFIELD_OP and for opcode_class AML_CLASS_UNKNOWN or AML_CLASS_ARGUMENT. It optionally displays the op (when output goes to a file, single-stepping is on, or ACPI_LV_PARSE is set), temporarily clearing op->common.next and the ACPI_LV_PARSE and ACPI_LV_FUNCTIONS debug levels and restoring them afterwards. It returns AE_OK if acpi_gbl_cm_single_step is FALSE; if acpi_gbl_step_to_next_call is set it returns AE_OK unless op is AML_INT_METHODCALL_OP (in which case the flag is cleared). For an AML_INT_METHODCALL_OP it clears acpi_gbl_cm_single_step and sets walk_state->method_breakpoint to 1. Finally it exits the interpreter, runs acpi_db_start_command(walk_state, op), re-enters the interpreter and returns the status of that call unchanged; that status is AE_OK when the loop resumes execution, AE_CTRL_TERMINATE when the user terminates, or another error from the command loop or OS notify calls.
note: Reviewer round 15 wrong: acpi_db_start_command returns its status unchanged (dbxface.c:86-90 only logs when status != AE_CTRL_TERMINATE) and acpi_db_single_step returns it (:375-380), so AE_CTRL_TERMINATE is returned as is. Round 2 (early AE_OK returns for step-to-next) now listed. Round 0 right that user breakpoint is not cleared (:244-251). Function at :201-381.

name: acpi_ds_call_control_method
prose: Sets up a nested control-method call from this_walk_state on thread; op is not used by this function (acpi_ds_init_aml_walk is passed NULL). It returns AE_NULL_ENTRY if this_walk_state->method_call_node is NULL, AE_NULL_OBJECT if that node has no attached object, AE_AML_TOO_FEW_ARGUMENTS if num_operands is less than the method's param_count and AE_AML_TOO_MANY_ARGUMENTS if it is greater. It then calls acpi_ds_begin_method_execution; if that fails its status is returned (AE_AML_METHOD_LIMIT, AE_AML_MUTEX_ORDER, or an error from creating or waiting on the method mutex or allocating an owner ID); in that case no new walk state is created and thread_count is not incremented, but the method mutex, the method's owner state and the thread's current_sync_level may have been changed by the partial work (an owner-ID failure releases the OS mutex if one exists without undoing the acquisition depth or thread_id). Otherwise it creates the new walk state with acpi_ds_create_walk_state (which pushes it on the thread when thread is non-NULL); if that fails it returns AE_NO_MEMORY after acpi_ds_terminate_control_method(obj_desc, NULL), which with a NULL walk state decrements thread_count and may release the owner ID but does not release the method mutex. It then sets operands[num_operands] to NULL (needs one spare slot) and allocates a zeroed evaluation info; if that allocation fails it returns AE_NO_MEMORY, after popping the walk state from the thread, terminating the method with that walk state and deleting it. It then calls acpi_ds_init_aml_walk, frees the info, and on failure returns its status through the same pop, terminate and delete cleanup. In none of these failures does it clear the caller's operands. On success it sets the new walk state's nesting depth, clears the caller's operands with acpi_ds_clear_operands, stores the result of acpi_ns_get_normalized_pathname (not NULL-checked) in this_walk_state->method_pathname, sets method_is_nested to TRUE and leaves the new walk state on the thread's stack. If the method is flagged ACPI_METHOD_INTERNAL_ONLY it calls its implementation and returns AE_CTRL_TERMINATE when that returns AE_OK, or the implementation's status otherwise (no method termination here); otherwise it returns AE_OK.
note: Reviewer round 15 wrong: op is unused; the call passes NULL (dsmethod.c:538) and op never appears in the body. Round 2 right that AE_NULL_ENTRY from begin is unreachable here since method_node is checked first (:476-478), and prose now only lists it for method_call_node. Earlier prose said cleanup with the NULL walk state releases the mutex: wrong, acpi_ds_terminate_control_method only does that inside its if(walk_state) block (:719-822). Function at :455-598.

name: acpi_ds_terminate_control_method
prose: Cleans up after one thread finishes executing a control method; returns void. If method_desc is NULL it returns immediately. If walk_state is non-NULL it first drops a RefOf return reference that points at one of the walk state's locals or arguments (removing the reference and clearing walk_state->return_desc), deletes all arguments and locals with acpi_ds_method_data_delete_all, and, when the method is not module-level and thread_count == 1, deletes the namespace subtree under walk_state->method_node and, if ACPI_METHOD_MODIFIED_NAMESPACE is set, the objects owned by owner_id (clearing that flag), temporarily leaving the interpreter around each deletion; then, if the method has a mutex, it decrements the acquisition depth and when it reaches 0 restores the thread's current_sync_level, releases the OS mutex and clears the mutex thread_id. These steps are skipped when walk_state is NULL. In all cases it then decrements method.thread_count (logging an error and leaving it at 0 if it was already 0). If threads remain, the owner_id is kept; if none remain, a pending serialization (ACPI_METHOD_SERIALIZED_PENDING) is converted to serialized with ignore-sync-level and sync_level 0, and the owner_id is released unless the method is module-level. Finally it calls acpi_ex_stop_trace_method.
note: Slice cut the head; real name acpi_ds_terminate_control_method (dsmethod.c:704-897), packet said acpi_ds_terminate_method and dropped it. Verified against source; mutex release is inside the if(walk_state) block (:807-821).

name: acpi_ds_create_operand
prose: Builds the operand for argument arg (position arg_index) and pushes it onto walk_state's operand (object) stack with acpi_ds_obj_stack_push; returns AE_OK on success. If arg is an AML_INT_NAMEPATH_OP with a non-NULL name string and is not in the parse stack, it gets the full name string with acpi_ex_get_name_string (returning its failure status), then either, for the deferred buffer-field name argument, uses walk_state->deferred_node, or looks the name up with acpi_ns_lookup (load-pass-2 mode when the parent op has AML_NSNODE and is not a method call, region or namepath, else execute mode); a lookup AE_NOT_FOUND becomes AE_OK with the root node for a ConditionalRefOf parent, AE_AML_BAD_OPCODE for an AML_EXTERNAL_OP parent, and AE_AML_NAME_NOT_FOUND otherwise, and other lookup errors are returned; the name string is freed after the lookup and the resulting node/object pointer is pushed (a push failure is returned). Otherwise (non-name argument, or a null namepath, treated as AML_ZERO_OP) it returns AE_NOT_IMPLEMENTED if the opcode's object type is ACPI_TYPE_INVALID; if the opcode returns a value or arg is in the parse stack it pops the previous result with acpi_ds_result_pop (returning its failure, for example a stack underflow, after logging); otherwise it creates an internal object (AE_NO_MEMORY on failure) and initialises it with acpi_ds_init_object_from_op, deleting it and returning the status if that fails. It then pushes the object onto the operand stack (returning a push failure) and returns AE_OK. No reference is added by this function when pushing.
note: Slice cut the head; function starts at dsutils.c:421. Reviewer round 15 wrong: results are pushed with acpi_ds_obj_stack_push (the operand stack, dsutils.c:565 and 636); the result stack is only popped (:603). Removed the unverified 'stack holds a reference' claim.

name: acpi_ds_load1_end_op
prose: Load-pass-1 ascending callback for the op in walk_state->op; returns an acpi_status. If ACPI_PARSE_DISASSEMBLE is set and the op has the AML_CREATE flag it returns the status of acpi_ds_create_buffer_field. It returns AE_OK if the op has neither AML_NAMED nor AML_FIELD. For a field op it returns AE_OK or, when not inside a method (walk_state->method_node NULL) and the opcode is Field, BankField or IndexField, the status of acpi_ds_init_field_objects. For other named ops, when not in a method: AML_REGION_OP and AML_DATA_REGION_OP create the region with acpi_ex_create_region and return its status on failure; an AML_NAME_OP with an argument takes its object type from the argument's opcode info and sets op->common.node->type when a node exists; and for AML_METHOD_OP, if the node has no attached object, it puts the node in operands[0], calls acpi_ds_create_operands and then acpi_ex_create_method, clears operands[0] and num_operands, and returns the failure status if either failed (an existing attached object is left untouched). (An ASL-compiler-only block handles AML_EXTERNAL_OP.) Finally, when not in a method, the opcode is not AML_EXTERNAL_OP and acpi_ns_opens_scope(object_type) is true, it pops the scope stack and returns the status of acpi_ds_scope_stack_pop; otherwise it returns AE_OK. The region-creation, operand and method-creation failure returns happen before the scope pop, so the scope is not popped on those paths.
note: Slice cut the head and the packet label (load2_end_op fragment) was wrong: slice is the tail of acpi_ds_load1_end_op (dswload.c:396-596), checked against the source. Systematic: packet name wrong. Fixed rather than dropped per rule 6.

name: acpi_ds_load2_begin_op
prose: Load-pass-2 descending callback. If walk_state->op is non-NULL and walk_state->control_state is in ACPI_CONTROL_CONDITIONAL_EXECUTING state it returns the status of acpi_ds_exec_begin_op(walk_state, out_op). If op is non-NULL and is not a namespace opcode (and not AML_INT_NAMEPATH_OP) or is not AML_NAMED, or is a namepath op with a NULL string, it returns AE_OK. The name comes from the op (or from the AML stream via acpi_ps_get_next_namestring when op is NULL). By opcode: Field, BankField and IndexField use node = NULL; AML_INT_NAMEPATH_OP does an acpi_ns_lookup in execute mode; AML_SCOPE_OP with an op whose named.node is the root pushes the scope for the root, otherwise does an execute-mode lookup (a failure logs and returns, except that under ACPI_ASL_COMPILER an AE_NOT_FOUND is turned into AE_OK and returned immediately), and then checks node->type: ANY, scope, Device, Power, Processor and Thermal are accepted, Integer, String and Buffer are changed to ACPI_TYPE_ANY with a warning (also setting walk_state->scope_info->common.value to ACPI_TYPE_ANY), a Method is accepted only for the root node during module-level code, and any other type returns AE_AML_OPERAND_TYPE. For all other opcodes, if op already has a node it pushes the scope when the object type opens one and returns AE_OK without touching *out_op; else it uses walk_state->deferred_node if set, or enters the name with acpi_ns_lookup in load-pass-2 mode (flags include prefix-must-exist for named ops, and in execute pass error-if-found and, outside module-level code, temporary). If a lookup or the other steps leave a failing status it logs and returns it (the failing sources are acpi_ds_exec_begin_op, acpi_ns_lookup and acpi_ds_scope_stack_push). If op was NULL it allocates a new op with acpi_ps_alloc_op (returning AE_NO_MEMORY if that fails), copies the node's name into it when node is non-NULL and stores it in *out_op. Finally it sets op->common.node to node (NULL for field opcodes) and returns the status (AE_OK).
note: Slice cut the head (function starts at dswload2.c:37). Reviewer round 15 wrong: field, processor, region and method object creation is done in acpi_ds_load2_end_op, not in this function, so there is nothing missing here. The existing-op-with-node path returns early (dswload2.c:237-252) and does not update op->common.node; earlier prose said it was updated for any existing op.

name: acpi_ev_gpe_dispatch
prose: Dispatches an active general purpose event; returns ACPI_INTERRUPT_HANDLED or ACPI_INTERRUPT_NOT_HANDLED. It is called by acpi_ev_detect_gpe with the GPE lock held. It first disables the GPE with acpi_hw_low_set_gpe(ACPI_GPE_DISABLE); if that fails it logs and returns ACPI_INTERRUPT_NOT_HANDLED. If the GPE is edge-triggered it then clears its status bit with acpi_hw_clear_gpe; if that fails it logs, re-enables the GPE with ACPI_GPE_CONDITIONAL_ENABLE and returns ACPI_INTERRUPT_NOT_HANDLED (disable_for_dispatch is not set on this path). Otherwise it sets gpe_event_info->disable_for_dispatch to TRUE and switches on the dispatch type: for an installed handler it calls the handler(gpe_device, gpe_number, context) and, if the handler's return value has ACPI_REENABLE_GPE set, calls acpi_ev_finish_gpe (its status ignored); for a method or notify dispatch it queues acpi_ev_asynch_execute_gpe_method with acpi_os_execute and, if queuing fails, only logs an error; if neither a handler nor a method is installed it logs an error. In all of these dispatch cases it returns ACPI_INTERRUPT_HANDLED, and the GPE is left disabled unless the handler asked for re-enabling or the asynchronous method later re-enables it.
note: Real name acpi_ev_gpe_dispatch (evgpe.c:747-849); packet name acpi_ev_dispatch_gpe does not exist. Slice cut the head. Prior prose omitted the initial disable and its failure return. Systematic: packet name wrong.

name: acpi_ex_opcode_1A_0T_1R
prose: Executes a one-operand AML opcode that returns a value, switching on walk_state->opcode with operand[0] = walk_state->operands[0]; returns an acpi_status. LNot creates an integer result that is ACPI_UINT64_MAX when operand[0]->integer.value is 0 and 0 otherwise (AE_NO_MEMORY if allocation fails). Increment and Decrement allocate an integer, resolve a temporary copy of the operand reference to an integer with acpi_ex_resolve_operands(AML_LOGICAL_NOT_OP, ...), set the result to that value plus or minus one (unsigned wrap-around is not checked), and store it back through operand[0] with acpi_ex_store, whose status is returned. ObjectType returns an integer holding the type from acpi_ex_resolve_multiple. SizeOf returns the integer byte width for an Integer, the length for a String, and the length or element count for a Buffer or Package (after acpi_ds_get_buffer_arguments or acpi_ds_get_package_arguments, whose failure status is returned); any other type gives AE_AML_OPERAND_TYPE. RefOf returns the reference built by acpi_ex_get_object_reference. DerefOf accepts a namespace node whose attached object is a String or a reference, a reference operand (local and argument references are first replaced by their current value, RefOf references by the object they point to) or a String; a String is looked up in the current scope with parent search and resolved to a value. Otherwise it returns the dereferenced object: for a named node, the node itself for Device and Thermal types or else the attached object with an added reference; for an Index reference into a buffer, a new integer holding the indexed byte; for an Index reference into a package, the element with an added reference, or an immediate return of AE_AML_UNINITIALIZED_ELEMENT if the element is NULL; for a RefOf reference, the target object (read through acpi_ex_read_data_from_field for buffer, region, bank and index fields, returning the read status immediately on failure, or with an added reference for other objects), or a NULL result with AE_OK when a named target has no attached object. Wrong operand kinds return AE_AML_OPERAND_TYPE (including an Index reference with an unknown target type), an unknown reference class returns AE_TYPE, and an unknown opcode returns AE_AML_BAD_OPCODE. At the common exit, on failure the return object's reference is released and walk_state->result_obj is left unchanged; on success walk_state->result_obj is set to the return object. The two immediate returns mentioned skip that exit step.
note: Slice is the middle of acpi_ex_opcode_1A_0T_1R (exoparg1.c:578-1086), cut head and tail; packet name acpi_ex_resolve_operands was wrong (that function lives in exresop.c). Fixed rather than dropped. Same function as the key exoparg1.c:1016-1086, so the prose is identical for both keys. Systematic: packet name wrong.

name: acpi_ex_resolve_operands
prose: Checks, and where needed converts, the operands on the stack for opcode; stack_ptr points to the topmost operand and is decremented for each further operand the opcode's runtime argument list needs. It returns AE_AML_BAD_OPCODE if the opcode's class is AML_CLASS_UNKNOWN, AE_AML_INTERNAL if the opcode has no valid argument-type list or a NULL stack entry is found, AE_AML_OPERAND_TYPE for an invalid object type, an unknown reference class, an invalid descriptor, or an operand whose resolved type does not match the required one (including when a convert helper returns AE_TYPE), AE_BAD_PARAMETER for an unknown argument type, and otherwise a status propagated from acpi_ex_check_object_type, acpi_ex_resolve_to_value or acpi_ex_convert_to_integer, _buffer or _string; it returns AE_OK once the whole argument list has been processed. For each operand: an alias node is replaced by its target in the stack slot; reference-style argument types (reference, integer-ref, object-ref, device-ref, target and store-target kinds, and a non-string for the reference-or-string type) are checked to be a namespace node or a reference but are not resolved to a value; a String for the reference-or-string type is accepted as is, and for the Store data-ref type an Index reference is also left unresolved. All other operands are resolved with acpi_ex_resolve_to_value and then checked against the argument type (mutex, event, package, any, ddb handle, integer, buffer, string, compute-data, buffer-or-string, data object, complex object, region-or-buffer, or the Store data-ref/Debug cases); Integer, Buffer and String arguments, and an Integer for the buffer-or-string type, are implicitly converted in place and the original object's reference is released when a replacement object was produced. On an error return, operands processed before it keep the changes made (aliases replaced, values resolved or converted).
note: Slice cut the head (function starts at exresop.c:98). Reviewer round 15 right: reference-type and some other operands are explicitly left unresolved (exresop.c:250-316). Earlier prose claimed ownership remains with the caller, which the code does not state; removed.

name: acpi_hw_register_read
prose: Reads one ACPI fixed register selected by register_id into *return_value and returns an acpi_status. For ACPI_REGISTER_PM1_STATUS and PM1_ENABLE it reads the A and optional B register blocks with acpi_hw_read_multiple and combines them (the two halves are ORed); for ACPI_REGISTER_PM1_CONTROL it does the same on the FADT control blocks and then clears ACPI_PM1_CONTROL_WRITEONLY_BITS from the value; for ACPI_REGISTER_PM2_CONTROL and ACPI_REGISTER_PM_TIMER it reads a 64-bit value with acpi_hw_read and keeps its low 32 bits; for ACPI_REGISTER_SMI_COMMAND_BLOCK it reads 8 bits from the SMI command port with acpi_hw_read_port. An unknown register_id logs an error and returns AE_BAD_PARAMETER. If the underlying read fails it returns that status. *return_value is written only when the status is a success; on AE_BAD_PARAMETER or a read failure it is left unchanged.
note: Slice cut the head (function starts at hwregs.c:488). Prior prose imprecisely said acpi_hw_read for PM1; PM1 goes through acpi_hw_read_multiple (:499-517). Behaviour of return_value verified at :558-560.

name: acpi_hw_legacy_wake
prose: Legacy-hardware (not ACPI_REDUCED_HARDWARE) cleanup after waking from sleep_state; returns an acpi_status. It sets acpi_gbl_sleep_type_a to ACPI_SLEEP_TYPE_INVALID and runs _SST with ACPI_SST_WAKING (the result of that call is ignored). It disables all GPEs with acpi_hw_disable_all_gpes and then enables all runtime GPEs with acpi_hw_enable_all_runtime_gpes; if either returns a failure, that status is returned at once, and the remaining steps (_WAK, clearing WAK_STS, setting acpi_gbl_system_awake_and_running, enabling and clearing the power-button and sleep-button events, and the final _SST) are not run. Otherwise it runs _WAK with sleep_state, clears the wake status bit, sets acpi_gbl_system_awake_and_running to TRUE, enables each of the power-button and sleep-button fixed events and clears their status bits (the results of these register writes are ignored), runs _SST with ACPI_SST_WORKING and returns the status from the GPE enabling call, which is AE_OK in that case.
note: Real name acpi_hw_legacy_wake (hwsleep.c:246-318); packet name acpi_leave_sleep_state is not in this file. Removed prior claim 'takes no locks': it calls GPE helpers that may lock. Systematic: packet name wrong.

name: acpi_ns_lookup
prose: Finds or enters pathname (internal AML namepath format, or NULL for the root) relative to scope_info and returns the node in *return_node. It returns AE_BAD_PARAMETER, writing nothing, if return_node is NULL; otherwise it sets *return_node to ACPI_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND and increments acpi_gbl_ns_lookup_count. It then returns AE_NO_NAMESPACE if acpi_gbl_root_node is NULL, AE_AML_INTERNAL if scope_info supplies a scope node that is not a namespace node, and AE_NOT_FOUND if the path has more parent prefixes than the starting node has ancestors. The starting node is the root for a root-prefixed or NULL path, else the scope node (moved up to an enclosing scope node unless ACPI_NS_PREFIX_IS_SCOPE is set), moved up once per parent prefix. For each name segment it calls acpi_ns_search_and_enter (execute mode for non-final segments when ACPI_NS_PREFIX_MUST_EXIST is set); a failure there returns its status with *return_node set to the node left in this_node (except that under ACPI_EXEC_APP an AE_ALREADY_EXISTS on a node flagged ANOBJ_NODE_EARLY_INIT is cleared and returned as AE_OK at once, and under ACPI_ASL_COMPILER with the disassembler flag an AE_ALREADY_EXISTS on an external node breaks out of the loop and continues as success). An intermediate alias node with no object returns AE_NOT_EXIST. A type mismatch on the last segment only logs a warning. After the segments, if ACPI_NS_DONT_OPEN_SCOPE is clear, walk_state is non-NULL and the resolved type opens a scope, it pushes the node on the scope stack with acpi_ds_scope_stack_push, returning that status (with *return_node still ACPI_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND) on failure. On success it stores the final node in *return_node and returns AE_OK. It assumes the caller holds the namespace lock.

name: acpi_ns_check_argument_count
prose: Checks the number of arguments a caller passed (user_param_count) and only emits messages; returns void and changes no state. If node->flags has ANOBJ_EVALUATED it returns at once. If predefined is NULL and the node is not a method, it logs an info message when user_param_count is non-zero and returns; if the node is a method it compares user_param_count with node->object->method.param_count and logs a warning for too few arguments or an info message for excess arguments. If predefined is non-NULL it takes the required count from predefined->info.argument_list and logs a warning when user_param_count is less, or an info message when it is greater unless ARG_COUNT_IS_MINIMUM is set in the argument list. It does not report an error to the caller.

name: acpi_ns_dump_one_object
prose: Namespace-walk callback that prints one node; context is a struct acpi_walk_info and the callback returns AE_OK on each of its return statements. It returns AE_OK without output if the info->debug_level bit is not set in acpi_dbg_level, if obj_handle is NULL, or if acpi_ns_validate_handle rejects it. Otherwise it increments info->count (before the owner check, so a node of another owner is still counted) and returns AE_OK without output when info->owner_id is not ACPI_OWNER_ID_MAX and differs from the node's owner_id. For a matching node it prints, depending on info->display_type, the indented node name, type, address and owner id, with acpi_dbg_level temporarily set to 0 while the attached object is fetched, then a type-specific description of the attached object (or '<No attached object>' for types that should have one) in summary mode, or reference-count and pointer details in object mode. If ACPI_LV_VALUES is set in acpi_dbg_level it also follows and dumps the chain of attached objects. It takes no lock and does not change the namespace; the side effects are output, the count increment and the temporary change of acpi_dbg_level.

name: acpi_ns_check_package
prose: Validates the Package in *return_object_ptr against the predefined-name entry that follows info->predefined; returns an acpi_status and may replace *return_object_ptr. It first calls acpi_ns_remove_null_elements, then if the package has no elements it returns AE_OK for ACPI_PTYPE1_VAR and otherwise warns and returns AE_AML_OPERAND_VALUE. It then switches on the expected type: custom packages go to acpi_ns_custom_package; PTYPE1_FIXED and PTYPE1_OPTION require at least the expected element count (else AE_AML_OPERAND_VALUE with a warning) and check element types; PTYPE1_VAR checks every element's type; PTYPE2_REV_FIXED requires an Integer first element and then checks the sub-packages; PTYPE2_PKG_COUNT requires an Integer first element whose value must be less than the element count (else AE_AML_OPERAND_VALUE) and checks that many sub-packages; PTYPE2, PTYPE2_FIXED, PTYPE2_MIN, PTYPE2_COUNT and PTYPE2_FIX_VAR wrap a package whose first element is not a package in a new outer package (acpi_ns_wrap_with_package, updating *return_object_ptr; a failure is returned) and check the sub-packages with acpi_ns_check_package_list; PTYPE2_VAR_VAR does no checking and returns AE_OK; PTYPE2_UUID_PAIR requires an even count (else AE_AML_OPERAND_VALUE), checks each (UUID buffer, object) pair and returns AE_AML_OPERAND_VALUE for a UUID buffer whose length is not 16; an unrecognised type returns AE_AML_INTERNAL. Failures from acpi_ns_check_object_type, acpi_ns_check_package_elements, acpi_ns_check_package_list, acpi_ns_custom_package and acpi_ns_wrap_with_package are returned unchanged.

name: acpi_ns_check_package_list
prose: Static helper that validates each of count sub-packages in elements against the expected type in package->ret_info.type; returns an acpi_status. For each sub-package it records it in info->parent_package, checks that it is a Package with acpi_ns_check_object_type (returning a failure) and then, by the expected type: PTYPE2, PTYPE2_PKG_COUNT and PTYPE2_REV_FIXED require at least count1 + count2 elements and check element types; PTYPE2_FIX_VAR requires count1 + count2 elements and checks the fixed part and the tail; PTYPE2_VAR_VAR does no element checks; PTYPE2_FIXED requires the fixed count and checks each element's type; PTYPE2_MIN requires at least count1 elements and checks all of them; PTYPE2_COUNT requires an Integer first element, a sub-package at least as large as that count and at least count1, and, if the stored count is 0, rewrites that Integer to the sub-package's element count before checking the remaining elements. A sub-package that is too small logs a warning with its index and returns AE_AML_OPERAND_VALUE; an unrecognised type returns AE_AML_INTERNAL; failures from the element checks are returned unchanged. It returns AE_OK after all sub-packages pass.

name: acpi_ps_get_next_arg
prose: Parses the next argument of type arg_type (an ARGP_* value) from parser_state; returns an acpi_status. On success it stores the new argument op (or NULL) in *return_arg. For ARGP_BYTEDATA, WORDDATA, DWORDDATA, CHARLIST, NAME and NAMESTRING it allocates an op and reads the value (AE_NO_MEMORY if the allocation fails). ARGP_PKGLENGTH sets parser_state->pkg_end and returns AE_AML_PACKAGE_LIMIT if the computed end is beyond aml_end or before aml (pkg_end has already been updated at that point); it yields NULL. For a non-empty ARGP_FIELDLIST it builds a list of field ops (freeing the partial list and returning AE_NO_MEMORY on failure) and skips aml to pkg_end; for a non-empty ARGP_BYTELIST it allocates one byte-list op. ARGP_SIMPLENAME, NAME_OR_REF, TARGET and SUPERNAME create an AML_INT_NAMEPATH_OP and parse the name path (freeing the op and returning the failure status if parsing fails) when the next opcode is 0, a leading name char, or a root or parent prefix; for TARGET and SUPERNAME, if the parsed op became a method call it frees the method-call op and its name sub-object, returns NULL and sets walk_state->arg_count to 1; when the next opcode is not a name start, walk_state->arg_count is set to 1 and NULL is returned. ARGP_DATAOBJ and TERMARG set walk_state->arg_count to 1 and return NULL; a non-empty ARGP_DATAOBJLIST, TERMLIST or OBJLIST sets arg_count to ACPI_VAR_ARGS and returns NULL. Any other arg_type logs an error, and returns AE_AML_OPERAND_TYPE with *return_arg set to NULL. On the early failure returns (no memory, package limit, name parse failure) *return_arg is not written; in the unknown-type failure it is written with NULL.
